ai.title: Fix spinner state management in checkpoint flow
ai.summary: Added explicit Spinner.get().stop() calls in checkpoint save and CLI prompt flow to prevent overlapping spinner states. Ensures 'Loading Files...' and 'Saving...' spinners terminate before 'Thinking...' starts. Covers npm-app/src/cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts and npm-app/src/cli.ts.

eli5.text: When you save your work or ask the assistant a question, you may briefly see a small spinning indicator (like 'Loading Files...', 'Saving...', or 'Thinking...'). Previously, these spinners could overlap and continue running at the same time, creating a confusing or cluttered display. This fix ensures each spinner stops cleanly before the next one starts, so you only see one smooth, sequential animation at a time. This makes the experience feel more polished and predictable.

ai.title: Fix WebSocket hang detection false positives
ai.summary: The `webSocketHangDetector` in `npm-app/src/rage-detectors.ts` now includes a `shouldFire` callback that checks the actual WebSocket state (`WebSocket.OPEN`) before triggering a rage event. This prevents false positives when a connection recovers during the 60-second timeout window. The `createTimeoutDetector` utility in `npm-app/src/utils/rage-detector.ts` was updated to support this optional async guard, and the `Client` class exposes `webSocket` publicly to facilitate the state check.

eli5.text: If your connection to the assistant briefly dropped and then recovered within 60 seconds, the software used to mistakenly assume the problem stuck around and log it as a serious failure. Now it double-checks whether the connection is still broken right when it records the problem, so a quick recovery no longer counts as a real failure. You wouldn't notice this directly unless you were watching the internal logs for these connection hiccups, which are now more accurate.

ai.title: Fix rage-detector test sleep mock
ai.summary: Added `sleep` mock for `@codebuff/common/util/promise` in `npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/rage-detector.test.ts`. Refactored `webSocketHangDetector` test to use `createTimeoutDetector` directly, bypassing complex `shouldFire` logic. Internal test stability fix for npm-app.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team fixed a flaky test that checks if the app wrongly detects a frozen connection. When you run the automated test, it sometimes failed at random because a fake delay (a 'sleep' mock) wasn't set up properly. Now the test directly checks the connection timeout logic without depending on a separate trigger condition, making it more reliable and faster to run. This is internal housekeeping only: no user sees or feels anything different.
